notes: Scenes tab (GM only): every map has a wall tag (WALLED, OPEN, PACK, BORDER, GM EDIT, NO WALLS) and the buttons above the list count and filter them. Click a tag to change it. Drawing walls by hand on an unfinished map marks it GM EDIT.
GMs always see the full hotbar; players keep the three-button bar.
Hotbar: just Market, Cyberdeck and Chrome. Empty slots are hidden (a GM sees them while hovering the bar); players also lose the page, lock, clear, mute and menu buttons.

Character sheets: the Spells tab is now the Quickhacks tab (quickhacks with Mk, RAM and loaded state, plus a button to the Cyberdeck); quickhacks no longer show as feats. Species and background slots are hidden. Credits are the only currency shown. The Cyberware Cache has a FEHA icon. Item hover cards are wide enough for their stats.
A gun that shares a name with a quickhack (Optic Zero) is no longer treated as a quickhack.

Prices: chrome within a Mk now follows impact (Sandevistans, Berserks, Second Heart and the Capacity Booster cost double; narrow utility pieces 40% less). Quickhacks cost 750 / 1,800 / 4,500 / 11,250 / 27,000 by Mk. Neural Adaptation Kit 7,500. Subdermal Plating reduces physical damage by 4.
Folders: the firearm catalog folder may be called FIREARMS and its maker folders by full company name; the PC folder is PLAYER CHARACTERS.

Combat test: quickhack and grenade once-per-turn limits, turn-based effect durations and the weapon fired-this-turn mark now follow the fight the character is in. With another encounter selected in the tracker (this world has a leftover active one), the limits were off and effects wore off after a few seconds.

Style pass: character and NPC sheets, roll dialogs, settings and configuration windows, notifications, the pause banner, tooltips and menus now use the FEHA black / red / yellow interface style (core-cp.css).
Content sweep: all 118 weapons fired, emptied and reloaded; all 20 quickhacks and all 18 grenade lines run from a player client.
Cookoff only lists real grenades (it offered guns) and Dead Trigger can break DMRs and LMGs.
Grenade result card no longer squeezes the target's name; the recon scan and EMP no longer treat guns as chrome.
A GM hot reload no longer removes FEHA's message handlers.

Release QA with three GMs and one player. Player quickhacks, player grenades and refund notices now reach the GM: FEHA messages no longer depend on the installed module's socket, which was never relayed.
With several GMs connected, grenade ticks, effect expiry, zone markers and armor bonuses are handled by the active GM only instead of once per GM.
Market: players only see their own characters and no reroll button; a copy of a bought item is no longer refunded as a duplicate purchase.
Weapon sheet redraws when a shot is spent; Cyberdeck quickhack names and the jack-in tray no longer overlap.

Bug test: opening the Chrome Manager for a character who owns cyberware no longer throws an error. The installed manager saved its slot and cost flags as if the chrome were a world item; those saves now go to the character.

Cyberarms are real weapons: Mantis Blades, Mantis Blades Apex, Monowire (Nano Wires), Power Grip Fists and Gorilla Arms appear in the inventory while the chrome is installed and leave when it is removed. Smart links add their bonus with Smart weapons; No Pain No Gain, Knife Sharpener and Blood Depleter add their bonuses to the roll automatically.

Cyberware capstones so every way of playing has Mk.IV-V chrome: Berserk C5, Mantis Blades Apex, Projectile Launcher Apex, Ballistic Coprocessor and the Corvus Apex Cyberdeck are new; Strong Arms, Kiroshi Optics Hunter, Chiton, Throwing Range Servos and the Rockerboy tattoo move to Mk.V; Sudden Aid can treat an ally. Camillo Ram Manager is once per rest.

NPC catalog: 29 ready-made people of Alabastra (street, Yakuza, CivCorp, Marble Vigil, corporate, Navy, civilians) built from the world's own weapons, armour, chrome and quickhacks. The GM imports them from a button in the Actors tab; nothing is created until then.
Looks pass: the chat log, dice results and pop-up dialogs use the same dark HUD style as the rest of the game; cyberware and consumable messages are proper cards.

Sandevistan is now a time stop: on activation you immediately take extra turns while nothing else can move, act or react (C1 a move and one attack; C2-C3 one turn; C4 two; Apogee three). C3 and up attack with advantage.

Cyberware rebuilt to follow Cyberpunk 2077 / Edgerunners: every item has a real effect, passive bonuses apply while installed, and active chrome (Sandevistan, Berserk, Kerenzikov, Blood Pump, Optical Camo...) spends CHARGE, which is the Cyberware Capacity you have left unused. Charge returns on a rest; with too little charge you can push past the limit for psychic damage.

Consumables now do what their card says when used from the character sheet: healing, temporary HP, RAM, or a timed bonus as an Active Effect. Once per Short Rest per product is enforced, a product that would be wasted is refused, and one item is used up. Ghost Key and Network Sweep are reworded as GM-run effects.

Text pass: screen labels no longer use tabletop words (scene, actor, token) or developer names; one name per thing (quickhack, signature, local net, credits). Market and Chrome Manager wording is corrected on screen by FEHA_UI_TEXT.

Network devices (hackable doors, turrets, terminals) are removed. The Cyberdeck has one CYBER CHECK button instead: 1d20 + Intelligence + proficiency, 1 RAM, rolled to chat; the GM sets the DC. Cameras are a GM tool: the Token controls have a Place camera button that drops a camera token owned by the chosen player, who sees through it.

Class-based reloads replace reload points: Pistol / Heavy Pistol / SMG / Shotgun Pistol reload with a Bonus Action; Assault Rifle / DMR / Shotgun / Bow and any single-shot weapon reload with an Action; LMG / Sniper Rifle reload takes a full turn (Action, no movement) plus a reload check (LMG Strength, Sniper Dexterity, DC = the weapon's STR requirement). A failed check means try again next turn. The weapon sheet shows one RELOAD button that rolls the check when needed.

STR requirement now matters: below it you attack with disadvantage (automatic) and can move only 10 ft on turns you use that weapon (table rule), unless installed Strong Arms / Power Grip / Reinforced Muscles / Gun Stabilizer, or any feat or cyberware flagged handling.negateStrRequirement, negates it.

LMG Brace: disadvantage if you moved more than 10 ft this turn (table rule). Sniper Scoped: automatic disadvantage against targets within 30 ft. Ashura and Long Vigil are close-range snipers (no scope penalty, 60/180 ft).
Feats or cyberware can set flags.fleshEnshrouded.handling.skipReloadCheck or reloadAdvantage.

Re-tune under the new reload model (LMG/sniper reload counted at 60% check success): 17 weapons changed, e.g. MA70 12d12, HMG 12d12, assault rifles +2d8, shotguns up, Black Requiem 7d20+28, Borg4a 29d6, Nekomata 4d20+54, Sunlance 1d20+90. Single hits are capped near 100 average; capped single-shot weapons keep their power rating so price reflects the alpha strike.
Disadvantage is applied through dnd5e.preRollAttackV2, so it works from the weapon sheet and the normal item roll.
